newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw bourse jumps, seen flat with focus on NFIs.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw bourse jumps, seen flat with focus on NFIs.

text.p: Polish shares jumped in higher trade but analysts expected prices to stabilise in the next few sessions with investor attention focused on National Investment Funds, which started bourse trade on Thursday.
The main market's WIG index rose two percent, to 16,437.0 and turnover rose five percent to 126.8 million zlotys ($39.6 million) on all three markets as 86 issues rose, 10 fell and nine were flat.

"The growth doesn't look like a longer-term tendency, I suspect investors will start selling soon and the market's attention shifts to NFIs," said Dariusz Szepieniec, analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
The NIF index, calculated as a sum of share prices of all 15 funds amounted to 160.0 points on Thursday.

Mass privatisation NFI units representing the NFIs traded at 150 zlotys ($46.9) in the single price auction system, but they rose later to 155 zlotys ($48.4) in the continuous trade and analysts expected arbitrage to make NFI units to converge with NFIs shares within the next few sessions.
Analysts said the bourse was likely to extend its 13-week sideways drift, still under pressure from large privatisations and forthcoming general elections due in September.

Bank Handlowy public offering now underway worth one billion zlotys ($312 million) and copper concern KGHM offering due to begin on June 30, worth at least 300 million zlotys ($93 million) were drawing investor capital and attention from the bourse, they said.
They said the 34.6-million-zloty ($10.8 million) trade in the NFIs was much higher than expected and they saw the funds trading mixed in the next sessions.
